parsed.explanation: The operative regime: no criminal exposure for a trans visitor since 2021, with statutory discrimination penalties (orientation-grounded, not enumerated for gender identity) and general constitutional rights. But documented police violence against a trans woman (June 2024) with custodial degrading treatment, under-investigated anti-LGBT violence, no gender-marker recognition (raising document-mismatch exposure at any identity check), no dedicated facilities, and social hostility (2005 ceremony condemned as 'shameless', 2010 ambassador refusal) place this below the acceptance-with-protections tier. The police-violence case shows state actors as perpetrators with recourse only beginning. Not near imprisonment-tier jurisdictions; conversely, remedies are unproven, so not above the 0.65 tier either.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific entry/visa rules documented, but no legal gender recognition domestically; whether foreign documents are doubted at borders is undocumented. Marker mismatch at any police ID check is a latent outing vector.
entry_documents.protection: No documented trans-specific entry bars or screening.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at a police stop could route into the documented police-custody pattern.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: June 2024: trans woman attacked by police for her gender identity, injured, arbitrarily detained, degrading treatment. No data on prison placement for trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Case is under investigation by judicial military police — recourse initiated but unproven.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arbitrary detention of a trans person by police is the documented operative escalation path if outed.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No shelters, safe houses or gender-neutral facilities recorded; facility practice for outed trans visitors undocumented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Absence of support infrastructure compounds any custody or care crisis.

care_services.exposure: Shadow report documents discrimination in health access; HIV-related care legally protected but general trans care access uncertain. Medication continuity undocumented.
care_services.protection: Legal entitlement to health care for people living with HIV; discrimination statute covers services by orientation.
care_services.interaction: A care encounter could out a visitor into the documented discriminatory environment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Police documented as perpetrators of identity-based violence; under-investigated violence per 2024 shadow report; 2010 refusal to receive gay ambassador signals official-level hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Discrimination criminalised with up to two years' imprisonment — a real statutory lever, though orientation-framed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Enforcement gap between statute and practice documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: No youth- or minor-specific findings on travel, medication or education recorded.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Under-investigated anti-LGBT violence documented; social hostility evidenced (2005 ceremony denounced in national media as 'shameless' and 'abominable'). No trans-specific violence counts or background rates to size it.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Visible trans presence accepted in mainstream culture (2012 singer profile); discrimination statute as recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to violence against trans victims is documented as weak.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Formal protection not matched by practice (2024 shadow report); section 87 civil-registration route untested for trans applicants; border practice undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active civil society (recognised NGO, regional and UN submissions) shows functioning advocacy channels.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist on paper; their operation for a visitor is unproven.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar administrative-tier consequences: friction, humiliation, possible detention without imprisonment or lethal threat. This jurisdiction's documented police assault on a trans woman is more severe than 0.55-B's screening delays, but its decriminalisation and criminalised discrimination are stronger mitigators; net comparable, slightly above on paper, slightly below in enforcement.

0.65-A has national equality protections plus police misconduct remedied with apology and compensation. Here the analogous police case is only under investigation with no shown outcome, and no enumerated gender-identity ground exists — so this sits below 0.65-A.

0.35-B features systematic targeted stops, confiscations and coerced interviews by policy. No such organised targeting is documented here; the 2024 police assault is a single documented case, not a stated pattern, and the statutory package is protective. Clearly above 0.35-B.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters a decriminalised jurisdiction with real statutory anti-discrimination penalties and general constitutional rights, but no enumerated gender-identity protection and no legal gender recognition, so identity documents can never match lived presentation locally — a standing outing vector at any ID check. The documented operative escalation if outed is the June 2024 pattern: police as perpetrators, arbitrary detention, degrading treatment, with recourse only nascent (military judicial police investigation) and violence under-investigated generally. Social climate adds hostility signals (media condemnation of a trans-visible ceremony, diplomatic refusal), partially offset by a visible mainstream trans cultural presence and active civil society. No entry bars, no organised sweeps, no credible imprisonment pathway documented. Consequences cluster in the harassment-to-arbitrary-detention range with thin, unproven remedies: mid-scale, around 0.55.
